Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Education | In Focus | National Mfantsipim School has a distinguished place in Ghana’s educational history – Vice President Source : Emmanuel Tetteh 14 November 2026 5:23pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Vice President Prof. Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has praised Mfantsipim School in the Central Region for its significant contribution to Ghana's educational development, describing the institution as an integral part of the country's formal secondary education history.
She said the school's 150-year journey had been marked by its commitment to nurturing generations of young men who had gone on to make meaningful contributions to society.
Speaking at the school's 150th anniversary celebration in Cape Coast on Saturday, November 14, the Vice President said Mfantsipim occupied a distinguished position in Ghana's educational history and deserved recognition for its longstanding contribution to the country's human resource development.
"Mfantsipim occupies a distinguished place in Ghana’s educational history. You are integral to the story of formal secondary education in this country. For 150 years, the school has nurtured generations of fine young men. We should be very proud of this," she said.
Prof. Opoku-Agyemang said the institution's longevity and achievements reflected the dedication of successive generations of educators, families and supporters who had contributed to sustaining its educational mission.
She noted that the school's impact extended beyond the classroom, having played an important role in shaping individuals who had contributed to different aspects of Ghanaian society.
The Vice President's remarks formed part of the recognition of Mfantsipim's enduring legacy as one of the country's historic secondary educational institutions.
She said the milestone was an opportunity not only to celebrate the school's achievements but also to acknowledge the people and institutions whose contributions had helped it maintain its reputation over the decades.
Prof. Opoku-Agyemang urged the school community to take pride in its history while recognising the responsibility of preserving its values and standards for generations.
The anniversary celebration brought together government officials, traditional authorities, religious leaders, alumni, education stakeholders, staff, students and other well-wishers to commemorate a century and a half of the institution's existence.
